text:
### Observed differences

- Four activities moved from partial to near-universal participation: before, A27 ran in about 54 in 100 traces and A36, A37 and A42 in about 46 in 100 each; in the later window each runs in about 99–100 in 100 traces, once per trace on average (mean occurrences about 1.0). A25, A26, A28 and A31 ran in every trace in both windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS001, POS002, POS004, POS005]
- Before, A36, A37 and A42 always appeared together as a block (in about 46 in 100 traces, internal order mixed) and were mutually exclusive with A27 (co-occurrence about 0–1 in 200); in the later window the block and A27 co-occur in about 99 in 100 traces, while the block's internal order remains mixed (about 52 vs 47 in 100 for A36 before A37). [REL011, REL012, REL013, REL020, REL021, REL022]
- Routing changed at three points: out of A25, transitions to A28 (about 98 in 100 before) were replaced by transitions to A36, A37 and A42 (about 35, 32 and 32 in 100); out of A26, the earlier split between A27 (about 54 in 100) and the block (about 45 combined) became almost exclusively A27 (about 98–99 in 100); and transitions from each block member to A31 (about 29–36 in 100 before) were no longer observed, replaced by transitions to A28 (about 30–36 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Order between the block and A26, A28 and A31 flipped: before, A26, A28 or A31 came first in about 46 in 100 of each pairing; in the later window the block activity comes first in about 99 in 100. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019]
- Event positions shifted accordingly: the block moved from a mean position of about 0.59 to about 0.40 of the trace, A28 from about 0.39 to 0.46, A26 from about 0.54 to 0.60, A27 from about 0.59 to 0.63 and A31 from about 0.63 to 0.66, with A25 roughly unchanged (about 0.36 to 0.35). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- Distances changed consistently: A28 followed A25 within one step in about 99 in 100 cases before but about four steps later in the later window (about 97 in 100), and A37 or A42 were within five steps of A31 in about 92 of 200 traces before but only 1 afterwards. [LAG001, LAG005, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the control flow around A25, A26, A27, A28, A31, A36, A37 and A42 was restructured. Before, the behaviour reads as A25 followed directly by A28, then A26 routing each case either to A27 (about 54 in 100) or to the block A36/A37/A42 (about 46), with A31 following whichever branch ran; in the later window it reads as A25 handing over to the block, all three block activities running in varying order before A28, A26 always leading to A27, and A31 following A27 — the former either/or choice became a joint, re-ordered pass through all of these activities. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, LAG001]

The support is direct and consistent: the successor profiles of A25, A26 and the block members show the re-routing, all six block-versus-{A26, A28, A31} orderings flip from about 46 to about 99 in 100, participation rises from about half of traces to essentially all traces, and the A25-to-A28 gap stretches from one to about four steps, matching the three activities now sitting between them. Forty-five items qualified against roughly 0.7 expected for an unchanged process, and every item's difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits; note, however, that the items largely describe one underlying restructuring rather than independent confirmations. [DIR001, DIR002, REL006, REL014, OCC001, OCC002, LAG001]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is sampling: with 200 traces per window, variant frequencies can differ without any change and a rare variant can appear in one window only, although differences of this size (participation up about 50 points, order preferences up about 50 points, successor profiles almost completely replaced) are difficult to produce by sampling alone. Positions and gaps are event positions, not clock time, so no timing claim is made; outgoing routing for A27, A28 and A31 is not part of the evidence, so the conclusion that A31 now follows A27 rests on order and gap evidence (A26 to A31 within two steps in about 96 in 100 later cases); and a few gap items rest on a single observation in one window and were not relied upon. [REL010, LAG003, LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
